system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: REVEAL NCT01252953 - REVEAL: Randomized EValuation of the Effects of Anacetrapib Through Lipid-modification
Investigational drug: anacetrapib
Document: Changes in lipoprotein subfraction concentration and composition in healthy individuals treated with the CETP inhibitor anacetrapib. (journal, published 2011-12-17, source pmid:22180633)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Changes in lipoprotein subfraction concentration and composition in healthy individuals treated with the CETP inhibitor anacetrapib.

We investigated the effects of the cholesteryl ester (CE) transfer protein inhibitor anacetrapib (ANA) on plasma lipids, lipoprotein subfraction concentrations, and lipoprotein composition in 30 healthy individuals. Participants (n = 30) were randomized to ANA 20 mg/day, 150 mg/day, or placebo for 2 weeks. Changes in concentration of lipoprotein subfractions were assessed using ion mobility, and compositional analyses were performed on fractions separated by density gradient ultracentrifugation. ANA 150 mg/day versus placebo resulted in significant decreases in LDL-cholesterol (26%) and apo B (29%) and increases in HDL-cholesterol (82%). Concentrations of medium and small VLDL, large intermediate density lipoprotein (IDL), and medium and small LDL (LDL2a, 2b, and 3a) decreased whereas levels of very small and dense LDL4b were increased. There was enrichment of triglycerides and reduction of CE in VLDL, IDL, and the densest LDL fraction. Levels of large buoyant HDL particles were substantially increased, and there was enrichment of CE, apo AI, and apoCIII, but not apoAII or apoE, in the mid-HDL density range. Changes in lipoprotein subfraction concentrations and composition with ANA 20 mg/day were similar to those for ANA 150 mg/day but were generally smaller in magnitude. The impact of these changes on cardiovascular risk remains to be determined.
--- END ---

Extract the facts.
